definitions.explanation: The sugar and starch components in food that serve as the body's primary energy source. In nutritional contexts, refers specifically to digestible carbohydrates excluding dietary fiber.

examples.japanese: {糖質|とうしつ}を{控|ひか}えている。
この{食品|しょくひん}は{糖質|とうしつ}が{少|すく}ないです。
examples.english: This food product is low in carbohydrates.

examples.japanese: {糖質|とうしつ}{制限|せいげん}ダイエットが{最近|さいきん}{流行|はや}っている。
examples.english: Low-carb diets have been popular recently.

notes:
USAGE:
{糖質|とうしつ} is the term commonly seen on Japanese nutrition labels and in diet-related discussions. It refers to digestible carbohydrates (sugars and starches), as opposed to {食物繊維|しょくもつせんい} (dietary fiber).

NUTRITION LABEL NOTE:
Japanese food labels list {炭水化物|たんすいかぶつ} (total carbohydrates) which equals {糖質|とうしつ} + {食物繊維|しょくもつせんい}.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {糖質|とうしつ}{制限|せいげん} (carb restriction, low-carb)
- {糖質|とうしつ}オフ (sugar-free/low-carb — used on product labels)
- {糖質|とうしつ}{量|りょう} (carbohydrate content)

RELATED NUTRITION TERMS:
- {脂質|ししつ} (lipids, fats)
- たんぱく{質|しつ} (protein)
- {炭水化物|たんすいかぶつ} (total carbohydrates, including fiber)
